name: CVM (cervical malformation)
summary: CVM, cervical vertebral malformation, also called cervical vertebral compressive myelopathy (CVCM) or wobbler syndrome: the neck vertebrae press on the spinal cord and a young horse becomes ataxic. Held here as a made-up recessive allele; treating it as one locus is a simplification made in this data, not a claim about horse genetics. UC Davis says a genetic part is likely but no causal mutation has been found and no DNA test exists; the evidence fits many genes plus environment - rapid growth, a rich diet, injury - rather than one allele. Thoroughbreds, Quarter Horses and Warmbloods are said to be predisposed, and males are affected more often than females. UC Davis advises not breeding affected horses.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: CVM (cervical malformation) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of cvm. The horse is completely normal and there is no way to see it - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way cervical vertebral malformation appears.

phenotypes.name: Cervical vertebral malformation
phenotypes.description: The neck vertebrae form or grow so that they press on the spinal cord: a young horse, often a fast-growing one, becomes ataxic - unsteady and uncoordinated, worst behind - a wobbler. How bad it gets varies; growth, diet and injury play a part.
